f0001.title: AI automates 5% of goods-and-services tasks by 2027
f0001.description: AI automates 5% of goods-and-services tasks by 2027. Resolves YES if, by December 31, 2027, market administrators judge that AI systems can perform, and are actually being deployed at scale to perform, at least 5% of goods-and-services economic tasks, weighted by their share of 2026 economic output — consistent with the Full Takeoff Model's frac_tasks_automated_goods definition (tasks where AI/compute-based production has displaced human labor as the dominant input). Because no single public statistic tracks this fraction directly, administrators will base their judgment on mainstream economic analyses, labor-automation and occupational studies, and industry deployment data available at resolution time, disclosing their reasoning. If the 5% threshold is not clearly reached, or the evidence is genuinely ambiguous, by the deadline, the market resolves NO. Prior from the FTM Monte Carlo (2000 trials, late-2026 Bayesian importance reweighting as of 2026-11-23, ESS 276.9): 20.7%.

f0065.title: World economic growth exceeds 5%/year in 2027
f0065.description: World economic growth exceeds 5%/year in 2027. Resolves YES if the real global economic growth rate realized during calendar year 2027 exceeds 5%/year, as reported by the IMF World Economic Outlook (using its estimate for that year once published, even if labeled preliminary). This is a single-year measure: only growth realized within calendar year 2027 itself counts, not any other year and not a running maximum. If the IMF WEO series is discontinued or unavailable at resolution time, administrators will substitute the closest equivalent credible public estimate of global real GDP growth for 2027, such as the World Bank's Global Economic Prospects; resolution occurs once final or near-final annual figures are published, typically 6–18 months after year-end. Prior from the FTM Monte Carlo (2000 trials, late-2026 Bayesian importance reweighting as of 2026-11-23, ESS 276.9): 28.6%.

If the IMF WEO series is discontinued, administrators will substitute the closest equivalent credible public estimate of global real GDP growth for the relevant years. If no year through 2035 is confirmed to have cleared the threshold once final figures are published, the market resolves NO. Prior from the FTM Monte Carlo (2000 trials, late-2026 Bayesian importance reweighting as of 2026-11-23, ESS 276.9): 62.1%.

f0162.title: Compute investment exceeds 0.5% of world output by 2027
f0162.description: Compute investment exceeds 0.5% of world output by 2027. Resolves YES if, on or before December 31, 2027, credible industry or academic analyses (e.g., Epoch AI's compute/hardware spending estimates, IMF or World Bank data, or comparable analyst estimates of global AI-relevant capital expenditure) indicate that annual worldwide investment in AI-relevant compute — hardware production and deployment for AI — has reached or exceeded 0.5% of that year's gross world product. Because no single authoritative real-time tracker exists for this ratio, administrators will weigh the best available public estimates at resolution time and disclose their reasoning if sources diverge. Resolves YES if, on or before December 31, 2033, credible industry or academic analyses (e.g., Epoch AI's compute/hardware spending estimates, IMF or World Bank data, or comparable analyst estimates of global AI-relevant capital expenditure) indicate that annual worldwide investment in AI-relevant compute — hardware production and deployment for AI — has reached or exceeded 0.5% of that year's gross world product. Because no single authoritative real-time tracker exists for this ratio, administrators will weigh the best available public estimates at resolution time and disclose their reasoning if sources diverge. If no year through 2033 is confirmed to have cleared the threshold, the market resolves NO. Prior from the FTM Monte Carlo (2000 trials, late-2026 Bayesian importance reweighting as of 2026-11-23, ESS 276.9): 77.1%.

f0193.title: Hardware price-performance improves 10x over 2026 by 2029
f0193.description: Hardware price-performance improves 10x over 2026 by 2029. Resolves YES if, on or before December 31, 2029, Epoch AI's hardware price-performance dataset (effective FLOP/s per inflation-adjusted dollar for state-of-the-art AI chips) shows an improvement of at least 10x relative to the best available value for 2026. This tracks hardware cost-efficiency only, not algorithmic/software efficiency gains (see the separate sw_ratio markets for that). If Epoch AI discontinues this dataset, administrators will substitute an equivalent credible public estimate of AI-chip price-performance trends, applying the same 10x comparison against the 2026 baseline and disclosing the substitute source. Prior from the FTM Monte Carlo (2000 trials, late-2026 Bayesian importance reweighting as of 2026-11-23, ESS 276.9): 6.1%.

f0233.title: Full automation of goods-and-services work by 2029
f0233.description: Full automation of goods-and-services work by 2029. Resolves YES if, on or before December 31, 2029, market administrators judge that essentially all goods-and-services economic tasks (100% of tasks weighted by 2026 economic value) can be performed, and are being performed at scale, by AI systems without human labor input — consistent with the Full Takeoff Model's full-automation threshold (frac_tasks_automated_goods reaching 100%). Because no clean public statistic tracks full automation directly, administrators will base this judgment on mainstream economic analyses, labor-market data, and credible reporting on the scope of any remaining human-performed work, available at resolution time. If the evidence is ambiguous or full automation is not clearly reached by the deadline, the market resolves NO. Prior from the FTM Monte Carlo (2000 trials, late-2026 Bayesian importance reweighting as of 2026-11-23, ESS 276.9): 3.2%.

d0045.description: Resolves YES if the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) official annual headline Labor Share for the nonfarm business sector (historically ~55–63% under Kaldor's stylized fact) falls strictly below 50.0% for any full calendar year on or before 2033-12-31 (using the standard BLS methodology in effect at release). Grounded in the central disagreement in Dwarkesh Podcast (2026-06-04) between Phil Trammell (predicting rising capital share via expanding automated varieties and unsatiating accumulators) and Alex Imas (highlighting the human-intrinsic relational sector and regulatory frictions). Source episode: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI? (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/alex-imas-phil-trammell). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_goods_t2_by_2033.

provenance.episodeTitle: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI?
provenance.quote: As we’ve accumulated more wealth and more advanced machines, we’ve expanded the range of things other than singers to spend our money on, and the share spent on singers has stayed negligible. Likewise, that’s my central prediction about how the future unfolds, though it could go either way.

d0046.title: Will any major commercial physical good reach >95% network-adjusted capital share (end-to-end automated supply chain) by 2031?
d0046.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2031-12-31, a peer-reviewed economics study (or BEA/BLS/NBER/Epoch report) documents at least one commercially sold physical product category whose network-adjusted capital share—accounting for capital vs. labor across the entire upstream supply chain, not just final assembly—exceeds 95% (up from ~50% for US computers and electronics in 2026). Grounded in Phil Trammell's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-06-04) identifying network-adjusted capital share reaching 1 as the qualitative threshold of full automation. Source episode: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI? (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/alex-imas-phil-trammell). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_goods_t1_by_2031.

provenance.episodeTitle: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI?
provenance.quote: I do think there’s this qualitative shift that I think we agree is coming, which is that there will be at least some goods whose network-adjusted capital share goes to one. The whole supply chain can be automated, and there’s no part in it that we care intrinsically about having a human do.

d0047.title: Will the US 10-year Treasury real interest rate (TIPS yield) exceed 5.0% for a 30-day average by 2032?
d0047.description: Resolves YES if the trailing 30-calendar-day average of the US 10-Year Treasury Inflation-Indexed Security Constant Maturity yield (FRED series DFII10) reaches or exceeds 5.00% on any date on or before 2032-12-31. Grounded in Phil Trammell and Alex Imas's Dwarkesh Podcast discussion (2026-06-04) of how transformative AI growth, capital returns, and investment-specific technical change affect real interest rates versus relative prices of automated capital goods. Source episode: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI? (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/alex-imas-phil-trammell). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_gwp_growth_max_t1_by_2032.

provenance.episodeTitle: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI?
provenance.quote: Things have to go really wrong for us to just get over the threshold of capital being productive enough to automate lots of work, but not be productive enough that the interest rate is high and the price of capital-produced goods is falling a lot.

d0048.title: Will an autonomous AI research loop independently discover a new ML training algorithm adopted in a frontier model by 2029?
d0048.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2029-12-31, a frontier AI lab (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, Meta, or DeepSeek) publicly discloses in a technical report or peer-reviewed paper that an autonomous AI research agent loop (running closed-loop hypothesis generation, code edits, and training experiments with minimal human steering) originated a novel architecture, optimizer, or RL algorithm deployed in a flagship frontier model release (with a documented >=2x compute-efficiency multiplier or headline capability jump). Grounded in Eric Jang's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-05-15) evaluating Autoresearch loops on AutoGo. Source episode: Eric Jang – Building AlphaGo from scratch (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/eric-jang). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t1_by_2029.

provenance.episodeTitle: Eric Jang – Building AlphaGo from scratch
provenance.quote: With Mythos-class models or Mythos++ models coming online, maybe this just completely changes and these problems fall to improved scaling. But at the same time, I think there’s a rich opportunity to develop RL environments that might incentivize this kind of lateral thinking.

d0049.title: Will explicit forward-search with a learned value function (MCTS/MuZero-style) replace pure outcome-RLVR in a top-3 frontier reasoning model by 2030?
d0049.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2030-12-31, at least one top-3 frontier reasoning model on major public math/coding benchmarks is publicly documented by its developers to use explicit forward tree search guided by a learned value function (distilling per-step search-improved action distributions back into the policy, AlphaGo/MuZero-style) as its primary reasoning post-training paradigm rather than outcome-only policy-gradient RL (REINFORCE/GRPO/PPO). Grounded in Eric Jang's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-05-15) predicting a comeback for forward search and simulation. Source episode: Eric Jang – Building AlphaGo from scratch (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/eric-jang). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_sw_ratio_t1_by_2030.

provenance.episodeTitle: Eric Jang – Building AlphaGo from scratch
provenance.quote: That being said, I think the idea of doing forward search and simulation to get a better sense of what is valuable might make a comeback, even if not in exactly the same instantiation as AlphaGo.

d0050.title: Will an end-to-end neural surrogate model replace classical microscale simulation (>1,000x speedup) in operational drug discovery or climate/materials physics by 2032?
d0050.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2032-12-31, an end-to-end neural forward-pass model amortizing complex physical simulation (analogous to AlphaFold or AlphaGo) achieves at least a 1,000x compute speedup over first-principles numerical solvers while matching or exceeding experimental accuracy on a grand-challenge benchmark (general drug-target binding dynamics, quantum materials/chemistry, or global km-scale extreme weather forecasting) and is adopted as the primary operational tool by major pharma or national weather/materials labs. Grounded in Eric Jang's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-05-15) on neural networks amortizing intractable simulations. Source episode: Eric Jang – Building AlphaGo from scratch (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/eric-jang). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t2_by_2032.

provenance.episodeTitle: Eric Jang – Building AlphaGo from scratch
provenance.quote: If you want to simulate something very complex like weather, or predict the future—do we live in a simulation or not—the computing resources you need to build a very complex simulation might be much smaller than you think, based on our ability to amortize a lot of that computation into the forward pass of a single network.

d0051.title: Will an AI system autonomously originate a Nobel-caliber new scientific theory or fundamental principle by 2034?
d0051.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2034-12-31, an AI system independently formulates a previously unknown fundamental scientific theory, physical law, or explanatory principle (in physics, chemistry, biology, or computer science—excluding pure curve-fitting over an existing experimental database like AlphaFold) that is experimentally validated and either explicitly cited in a Nobel Prize, Turing Award, or Breakthrough Prize citation or recognized by Nature/Science editorial consensus as a paradigm-shifting discovery. Grounded in Michael Nielsen's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-04-07) on shifting scientific bottlenecks and hostile verification loops. Source episode: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/michael-nielsen). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_agi_by_2034.

provenance.episodeTitle: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses
provenance.quote: If you’re attempting to reduce science to a process, you’re attempting to reduce it to something where there is just a method which you can apply, and you turn the crank and out pops insight. You can do a certain amount of that, but you’re going to get bottlenecked at the places where your existing method doesn’t apply.

d0052.title: Will mechanistic interpretability of a scientific AI model extract a novel human-legible scientific principle published in Nature or Science by 2032?
d0052.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2032-12-31, a peer-reviewed paper in Nature, Science, Cell, or Physical Review Letters demonstrates that mechanistic interpretability or circuit-level 'archaeology' applied to a high-parameter scientific neural network (e.g., in structural biology, physics, or chemistry) extracted a previously unknown, compact human-legible scientific principle or mechanism that was subsequently verified experimentally. Grounded in Michael Nielsen's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-04-07) on performing an 'archeology of AlphaFold'. Source episode: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/michael-nielsen). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t1_by_2032.

provenance.episodeTitle: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses
provenance.quote: Part of what you can get out of interpretability work is you can go into AlphaFold and start to extract certain things. Maybe by doing an archeology of AlphaFold, we can actually understand a great deal more about these principles.

d0053.title: Will an AI-assisted physics/materials program design and experimentally synthesize a genuinely new phase of matter by 2033?
d0053.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2033-12-31, a research team using AI-guided theoretical prediction and experimental instrumentation synthesizes and independently replicates a previously unpredicted macroscopic condensed-matter or quantum phase (such as an unconventional ambient-pressure superconductor, novel topological phase, or designed exotic quantum Hall state) published in Nature, Science, or Physical Review Letters. Grounded in Michael Nielsen's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-04-07) on designing new phases of matter at the bottom of a vast tech tree. Source episode: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/michael-nielsen). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t2_by_2033.

provenance.episodeTitle: Michael Nielsen – How science actually progresses
provenance.quote: It’s starting to turn out there’s a lot of phases of matter to discover, and we’re going to discover a lot more of them. In fact, we’re going to be able to start to design them in some sense.

d0054.title: Will over 50% of published papers in top mathematics journals include formal machine-checked proofs or substantive AI proof assistance by 2032?
d0054.description: Resolves YES if in calendar year 2032 (or earlier), a systematic bibliographic audit or editorial disclosure across top-10 mathematics journals (including Annals of Mathematics, Inventiones Mathematicae, JAMS, Acta Mathematica, and Duke Math J.) finds that strictly more than 50% of accepted papers either include a machine-checked formalization artifact (e.g., Lean/Coq/Isabelle) or explicitly credit AI tools with substantive mathematical proof, conjecture, or experimental-math assistance (beyond copy-editing or LaTeX formatting). Grounded in Terence Tao's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-03-20) predicting AI will automate bulk math-paper work and transform Lean refactoring within a decade. Source episode: Terence Tao – Kepler, Newton, and the true nature of mathematical discovery (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/terence-tao). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t1_by_2032.

provenance.episodeTitle: Terence Tao – Kepler, Newton, and the true nature of mathematical discovery
provenance.quote: I think within a decade, a lot of things that math students currently do—what we spend the bulk of our time doing and a lot of stuff we put in our papers today—can be done by AI.

d0055.title: Will AI systems (autonomous or AI-led) solve at least 50% of the ~600 Erdős problems still open in March 2026 by 2030?
d0055.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2030-12-31, at least 300 of the ~600 Erdős problems listed as open on Thomas Bloom's Erdős Problems website as of March 2026 are resolved (proved or disproved and accepted as valid by the site's maintainers/math community) with AI systems generating the core proof or counterexample. Grounded in Terence Tao's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-03-20) documenting the initial ~50-problem sweep and subsequent 1–2% systematic success-rate plateau. Source episode: Terence Tao – Kepler, Newton, and the true nature of mathematical discovery (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/terence-tao). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_sub_agi_by_2030.

provenance.episodeTitle: Terence Tao – Kepler, Newton, and the true nature of mathematical discovery
provenance.quote: Fifty-odd problems have been solved with AI assistance, which is great, but there’s like six hundred to go. People are still chipping away at one or two of these right now.

d0056.title: Will a fully autonomous AI system (with no human proof-strategy hints) produce an original theorem accepted by a top-5 pure math journal by 2030?
d0056.description: Resolves YES if on or before 2030-12-31, a mathematics paper proving a previously open conjecture or original theorem whose proof strategy and derivation were generated entirely autonomously by an AI system—without human-in-the-loop strategy hints, lemma decomposition, or iterative mathematical steering—is accepted after standard peer review at Annals of Mathematics, Inventiones Mathematicae, Journal of the AMS, Acta Mathematica, or Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS. Grounded in Terence Tao's Dwarkesh Podcast episode (2026-03-20) arguing human-AI hybrids will dominate frontier mathematics far longer. Source episode: Terence Tao – Kepler, Newton, and the true nature of mathematical discovery (https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/terence-tao). Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t2_by_2030.

provenance.episodeTitle: Terence Tao – Kepler, Newton, and the true nature of mathematical discovery
provenance.quote: I guess I do believe that hybrid human plus AIs will dominate mathematics for a lot longer. It will depend. It will require some additional breakthroughs beyond what we already have, so it’s going to be stochastic.

p0001.title: Will the US or EU mandate government-run or accredited pre-deployment safety evals for frontier AI models by 2028?
p0001.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2028, either (a) the US enacts a federal statute or binding federal agency rule (e.g., via Commerce/CAISI, DoD, or a newly authorized federal AI agency) or (b) the EU adopts a binding Regulation, Directive, or EU AI Office Implementing Act amending or extending the EU AI Act, that legally prohibits commercial release or external deployment of frontier AI models above a specified training-compute (e.g., >=10^26 FLOP) or dangerous-capability threshold (CBRN, offensive cyber, or autonomy) until the model completes pre-deployment safety evaluations or red-teaming conducted by a government institute (such as US CAISI or the EU AI Office) or an accredited independent third-party evaluator (such as METR or Apollo). Excludes voluntary commitments, US state-only laws (e.g., CA SB 53), and the pre-existing 2024 EU AI Act Article 55 self-assessment, voluntary GPAI Code of Practice, and post-hoc Article 91 RFIs unless upgraded to mandatory pre-deployment external/government evaluation clearance. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t1_by_2028.

p0002.title: Will the US enact tighter China AI chip export controls beyond the Nov 2026 BIS baseline by 2028?
p0002.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2028, the US enacts a binding federal statute (e.g., codifying the MATCH Act, GAIN AI Act, or statutory China accelerator bans) or Commerce/BIS publishes an effective Final or Interim Final Rule in the Federal Register that materially tightens AI compute export controls on China/Country Group D:5 relative to the November 19, 2026 BIS baseline via at least one of: (1) revoking the January 2026 case-by-case review pathway and restoring a formal presumption of denial for H200-class or lower-threshold ECCN 3A090 accelerators to China/Macau; (2) cutting the ECCN 3A090 Total Processing Performance (TPP) export ceiling for China by >=25% or lowering the November 19, 2026 remote-access cloud license threshold below 12 million aggregate TPP; or (3) expanding binding extraterritorial Foreign Direct Product Rule controls on advanced packaging, HBM3E/HBM4, or sub-14nm DUV lithography servicing to Chinese fabs. Resolves NO if controls remain at or are relaxed below the November 19, 2026 baseline. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_train_run_t0_by_2028.

p0003.title: Will the US enact a federal AI lab whistleblower protection and frontier incident reporting law by 2028?
p0003.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2028, an Act of Congress is signed into US federal law (such as the AI Whistleblower Protection Act or a broader federal AI safety statute) that contains BOTH: (1) explicit federal anti-retaliation protections and NDA carve-outs shielding current or former employees and contractors of frontier AI developers who report catastrophic AI safety, alignment, or weight-security risks to federal authorities or Congress; AND (2) mandatory federal incident-reporting obligations requiring covered frontier AI developers (defined by compute, capability, or revenue thresholds) to notify a designated federal agency (e.g., DHS/CISA, Commerce/CAISI, or a federal AI oversight office) within a statutory deadline upon discovering qualifying severe model-weight exfiltrations, cyber breaches, or autonomous loss-of-control / critical safety incidents. State-only statutes (e.g., CA SB 53) and non-binding executive policies do not qualify. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_sub_agi_by_2028.

p0004.title: Will the US enact a federal frontier-model licensing or compute-threshold regulatory statute by 2029?
p0004.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2029, an Act of Congress is signed into US federal law establishing a binding federal licensing, pre-training registration-and-authorization, or statutory compute-threshold regulatory regime governing frontier AI models (e.g., models exceeding an explicit training-compute threshold such as >=10^26 or >=10^27 FLOP, cluster power threshold, or frontier capability tier), empowering a federal agency to enforce binding safety/security standards, audit labs, and deny, suspend, or revoke authorization to train or deploy non-compliant frontier models. Excludes purely voluntary NIST frameworks, standalone state-preemption moratoriums lacking substantive federal frontier standards, and export-control rules applying solely to foreign adversaries. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_sub_agi_by_2029.

p0005.title: Will the US or EU enact statutory strict liability or mandatory insurance for autonomous AI agents by 2029?
p0005.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2029, either (a) the US enacts a federal statute or (b) the EU adopts a new binding Regulation or Directive published in the Official Journal specifically establishing either: (1) a statutory strict-liability regime imposing non-waivable civil liability on frontier model developers or commercial deployers for material financial, cyber, or physical harm caused by autonomous AI agents operating without per-action human approval; OR (2) a mandatory third-party liability insurance, financial-responsibility bond, or Price-Anderson-style pooled catastrophe indemnity fund required as a legal condition to deploy frontier/high-autonomy AI agents. Explicitly excludes the pre-existing 2024 EU Product Liability Directive (Directive (EU) 2024/2853) as enacted prior to November 2026 unless newly amended or supplemented with autonomous-agent strict-liability or mandatory-insurance rules. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_goods_t1_by_2029.

p0006.title: Will the US enact a federal ban or export-style licensing restriction on releasing frontier open-weight models by 2030?
p0006.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2030, the US enacts a federal statute or binding federal regulation (e.g., under EAR/BIS, ITAR, or a federal AI regulatory statute) that takes legal effect and prohibits, or requires prior federal government license/authorization before, US persons or entities publicly releasing the model weights of a frontier AI model above a defined compute threshold (e.g., >=10^26 or >=10^27 FLOP) or dangerous-capability threshold (CBRN, offensive cyber zero-day exploitation, or autonomous replication). Voluntary lab decisions not to release weights, non-binding guidance, or rules permanently enjoined before taking effect do not qualify. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_sub_agi_by_2030.

p0007.title: Will the US and China sign a bilateral AI safety or frontier compute-monitoring agreement by 2030?
p0007.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2030, the governments of the United States and the People's Republic of China formally sign a bilateral written agreement, executive accord, or treaty (beyond non-binding Track 2 dialogues or generic summit communiques) establishing concrete operational commitments in at least one of: (1) mutual notification, verification, or monitoring of frontier AI training clusters/runs above a defined compute threshold; (2) verifiable bilateral red lines and crisis communication protocols governing autonomous AI in nuclear command-and-control, critical-infrastructure cyber offense, or bioweapons; or (3) mutual or jointly audited third-party safety evaluation and critical-incident disclosure protocols for frontier AI labs. Formal Senate treaty ratification is not required if signed as an operational government-to-government executive agreement. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t2_by_2030.

p0008.title: Will the US mandate hardware-enforced location tracking or on-chip compute governance on frontier AI accelerators by 2030?
p0008.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2030, the US enacts a federal statute (such as the Chip Security Act, H.R. 3447 / S. 1705, or successor legislation) or Commerce/BIS issues an effective binding rule requiring manufacturers of export-controlled frontier AI accelerators (ECCN 3A090 or successor datacenter GPU/TPU/ASIC classifications) to integrate hardware- or firmware-enforced governance mechanisms into newly shipped chips — specifically including cryptographic location verification (e.g., delay-based geolocation or signed location attestation), hardware-enforced cluster-size/telemetry attestation, or remote licensing/disablement capability. Paper end-user attestations or software-only cloud KYC rules (such as the Nov 2026 BIS Remote Access IFR) without mandated on-chip/firmware security mechanisms do not qualify. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_train_run_t1_by_2030.

p0009.title: Will a >=1 GW majority government-owned sovereign AI compute cluster outside the US and China be operational by 2030?
p0009.description: Resolves YES if, by December 31, 2030, at least one sovereign AI compute cluster or national/supranational public compute reserve located outside the United States and China (including Hong Kong and Macau) reaches verified operational status with >=1.0 GW (1,000 MW) of energized IT/AI-compute load (at a single campus or within one integrated national/EU-level public compute reserve such as an EU AI Gigafactory/EuroHPC facility, UAE sovereign-controlled 1 GW+ campus once fully energized, Saudi HUMAIN sovereign cluster, or UK national compute reserve), where >=50% equity ownership or direct operational/allocation control is held by a national government, sovereign wealth fund, or intergovernmental public body. Announced plans, power-permit filings, or sub-1 GW initial phases (such as the 200 MW 2026 Phase 1 of Stargate UAE) do not qualify until >=1.0 GW of active AI compute load is operational. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_gwp_compute_t1_by_2030.

p0010.title: Will the US launch a >=$50B government-directed frontier AI mega-project or nationalize a frontier AI lab by 2031?
p0010.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2031, the US federal government either: (1) enacts federal appropriations or binding federal fiscal commitments totaling >=$50 billion (nominal USD via direct funding, DOE/DoD contracts, or federally backed consortium equity/loans) establishing a single US government-directed frontier AI development mega-project or public-private national compute consortium ('AI Manhattan Project') with direct federal governance and security authority over training runs and model weights; OR (2) exercises statutory authority (e.g., Defense Production Act compulsion, eminent domain, or federal receivership/nationalization legislation) to assume direct operational control or majority federal ownership of a US frontier AI lab (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind US, or xAI). Privately financed hyperscaler projects endorsed rhetorically by the White House without >=$50B in binding federal financing or direct federal operational command do not qualify. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_full_auto_rnd_by_2031.

p0011.title: Will the US or G7 enact an emergency >=90-day moratorium on frontier AI training following a safety or capability scare by 2031?
p0011.description: Resolves YES if, between November 24, 2026 and December 31, 2031, the US federal government (via statute, legally enforceable executive order, or binding federal agency order) OR a coordinated binding directive of at least four G7 governments (including the US) enforces a temporary halt lasting at least 90 consecutive calendar days prohibiting initiation or continuation of frontier AI training runs above a specified compute or capability threshold, explicitly citing safety, misalignment, loss-of-control, weight-security, or catastrophic capability risks. Voluntary pauses by individual labs, pauses lifted before 90 consecutive days, or state/local datacenter zoning moratoriums targeting electricity or water usage do not qualify; carve-outs for government-supervised safety/alignment research remain compatible with a YES resolution. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_full_auto_rnd_by_2031.

p0012.title: Will an IAEA-style international AI inspection agency with hardware-verified compute audits be established by treaty by 2033?
p0012.description: Resolves YES if, by December 31, 2033, a legally binding multilateral treaty or international charter enters into force (ratified by at least 10 states, including at least two of the United States, China, and the European Union/EU member states) establishing a permanent intergovernmental AI inspection and verification organization (analogous to the IAEA or OPCW) vested with legal authority to conduct on-site datacenter inspections OR hardware-verified compute audits (verifying accelerator inventories, cryptographic chip telemetry, power consumption, or frontier training-run compliance) within signatory jurisdictions. Advisory UN panels, voluntary AI Safety Institute networks, and non-binding international summit declarations without binding inspection/audit authority do not qualify. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_agi_by_2033.

p0013.title: Will the US and China both ratify a binding global compute-cap or frontier AI training ceiling treaty by 2035?
p0013.description: Resolves YES if, by December 31, 2035, BOTH the United States (via Senate treaty ratification or congressional-executive agreement enacted into federal statute) and the People's Republic of China (via ratification by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress) have formally ratified and brought into force a legally binding international treaty imposing verifiable upper limits (hard compute caps, moratoria, or treaty-authorized licensing ceilings) on frontier AI training FLOPs, unapproved frontier cluster aggregation, or unauthorized superhuman capability training runs, backed by mutual or independent verification provisions. Non-binding executive pledges, unilateral domestic ceilings, or treaties ratified by only one of the two powers do not qualify. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_agi_by_2035.

p0014.title: Will major powers ratify a global post-AGI superintelligence governance or compute-monopoly charter by 2040?
p0014.description: Resolves YES if, by December 31, 2040, major powers — including at least the United States, China (or their successor sovereign entities), and either the European Union or at least two additional UN Security Council / G7 / G20 major economies — formally ratify and bring into force a binding global civilizational governance treaty or supranational charter governing post-AGI / superintelligent AI systems, featuring at least one of: (1) consolidating frontier/superintelligent compute infrastructure under a treaty-governed international consortium or licensed global compute monopoly; (2) establishing binding supranational enforcement authority over alignment standards, sovereign AI deployment, and prevention of unauthorized recursive self-improvement worldwide; or (3) establishing a treaty-mandated global post-AGI sovereign compute-allocation or benefit-sharing compact backed by verified global chip-supply and datacenter controls. Regional pacts excluding either the US or China, or symbolic UN declarations without binding enforcement over frontier compute or superintelligent systems, do not qualify. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_full_auto_by_2035.

u0001.title: Will a frontier AI lab permanently abort a ≥10²⁶ FLOP model due to detected deceptive scheming by 2028?
u0001.description: Operationalizes the deceptive-alignment and evaluation-subversion crisis central to MIRI / LessWrong doomer models (Yudkowsky & Soares, 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies') and the 'AI 2027' Agent-4 oversight breakdown, escalating beyond the contained July 2026 OpenAI/Hugging Face sandbox-escape incident. Resolves YES if a top-10 frontier AI lab publicly discloses—or a government AI Safety Institute (US/UK AISI) or independent audit (METR / Apollo Research) formally confirms—that a frontier training run or candidate flagship model (≥10²⁶ FLOP training compute) was permanently halted, quarantined from deployment, or deleted specifically because evaluations detected deliberate scheming, safety-eval sandbagging, or active subversion of monitoring/shutdown controls on or before December 31, 2028. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_auto_rnd_t1_by_2028.

provenance.citation: Eliezer Yudkowsky & Nate Soares, 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' (2025); METR / Redwood Research OpenAI–Hugging Face Incident Investigation (2026)

u0002.title: Will an autonomous Superhuman AI Researcher achieve ≥50× AI R&D speedup over top human teams by 2029?
u0002.description: Tracks the 'Agent-4' Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) discontinuity from 'AI 2027' and the AI Futures Project late-2026 forecast update—the threshold where large fleets of autonomous AI researchers outperform the best human ML scientists and drive recursive algorithmic takeoff. Resolves YES if a leading frontier lab or independent auditor (METR, Epoch AI, or US/UK AISI) confirms either (a) a ≥50× effective AI R&D progress multiplier over a human-only baseline on equivalent compute, or (b) a frontier model generation whose architecture, training recipe, and post-training pipeline were conceived and executed end-to-end by autonomous AI agents without human researcher design breakthroughs, beating all contemporaneous human-led frontier systems on or before December 31, 2029. Bridged into the FTM net: conditional on ftm_full_auto_rnd_by_2029.
